title: Spaghetti Bolognese
blurb: The long-simmered weeknight standard: beef, soffritto, tomato, time.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil over low heat for 10 minutes until sweet and translucent.
Raise the heat, add the beef and brown it properly — let it sit undisturbed until it catches, then break it up.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for two minutes until the paste darkens.
Pour in the wine and let it reduce almost away, then add the tinned tomatoes and the milk.
Simmer uncovered for at least an hour, stirring now and then. Season at the end, not the beginning.
Cook the spaghetti, toss it through the sauce with a splash of pasta water, and finish with parmesan.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
blurb: Charred marinated chicken in a spiced tomato and cream sauce.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, half the spices, the ginger and half the garlic. An hour minimum, overnight if you can.
Grill or broil the chicken on a rack until the edges char. This char is the whole dish; do not skip it.
Meanwhile soften the onion in oil, add the remaining garlic and spices and fry for a minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, then blend smooth if you like it that way.
Stir in the cream, return the charred chicken to the pan and simmer 10 minutes more.
Serve over rice with cilantro.

title: Ground Beef Tacos
blurb: Twenty minutes, one pan, and everything else goes on the table in bowls.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Brown the beef hard in a dry pan, breaking it up only once it has colour.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then the garlic, spices and tomato paste. Two minutes.
Splash in a little water and let it reduce to a glossy sauce.
Warm the tortillas directly over a flame or in a dry pan until they blister.
Put everything on the table and let people build their own.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
blurb: The one you make when someone is ill, or when it is raining.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, thyme and bay, then pour in the stock and bring to a bare simmer.
Poach the chicken in the broth for 15 minutes, then lift it out and shred it.
Cook the noodles in the broth, return the chicken, and season.
Finish with parsley and a squeeze of lemon — the lemon is what makes it taste like more than salt.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
blurb: Four ingredients, no cream, and a great deal of nerve.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Render the bacon slowly in a cold pan until the fat runs and the edges crisp.
Beat the eggs with the parmesan and a great deal of black pepper.
Cook the spaghetti, reserving a mugful of the water.
Off the heat, toss the drained pasta through the bacon fat, then the egg mixture, loosening with pasta water.
Keep it moving. The residual heat cooks the sauce; direct heat scrambles it.

title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken
blurb: Coconut, chili and basil, on the table in half an hour.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.

ingredients.note: check the label — most contain shrimp paste
thai basil if you can find it

steps: Fry the curry paste in the oil for a minute until it smells like something.
Add the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk can and let it split slightly.
Add the chicken and turn it through the paste, then pour in the rest of the coconut milk.
Simmer 10 minutes, add the vegetables and cook 5 more.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and lime — taste, adjust, taste again. Basil off the heat.

title: Smash Burger
blurb: Thin patties, a screaming hot pan, and a crust you can hear.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Divide the beef into four loose balls. Do not season yet and do not compact them.
Get a heavy pan or griddle as hot as it will go. Oil it barely.
Press each ball flat with a spatula and hold for ten seconds. Salt the top.
Flip once the edges are lacy and dark, add cheese, and cover for thirty seconds.
Toast the buns in the fat left behind. Build, and eat immediately.

title: Chicken Caesar Salad
blurb: Anchovy, garlic and parmesan doing all the work.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Toss the bread cubes in oil and salt and roast at 200°C until they are dark at the corners.
Season and pan-sear the chicken, then rest it and slice thickly.
Mash the anchovies and garlic to a paste, then whisk in the yolk, mustard, mayo, lemon and grated parmesan.
Dress the lettuce more heavily than feels right; caesar is a dressing dish.
Top with the chicken, the croutons, and more parmesan.

title: Pork Ramen
blurb: A rich pork broth, a jammy egg, and noodles with bite.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Brown the pork on all sides, then simmer it in the stock with the garlic, ginger and mushrooms for 90 minutes.
Soft-boil the eggs for six and a half minutes, peel, and steep them in soy sauce.
Lift out the pork, slice it, and whisk the miso into the hot broth off the boil.
Cook the noodles separately — always separately, or the broth goes cloudy with starch.
Build each bowl: noodles, broth, pork, egg, corn, scallion, a few drops of sesame oil.

title: Shrimp Scampi
blurb: Garlic, butter, white wine, lemon. Fifteen minutes.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Start the pasta. Everything else takes less time than the water takes to boil.
Sizzle the garlic and chili gently in the oil and half the butter. Do not let the garlic brown.
Add the shrimp in one layer and cook two minutes a side, no more.
Deglaze with the wine, let it bubble down, then swirl in the rest of the butter and the lemon.
Toss with the drained pasta and a splash of its water, and finish with parsley.

title: Teriyaki Salmon
blurb: A glaze that reduces in the time the fish takes to cook.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Whisk the soy, maple, vinegar, ginger, garlic and cornstarch together.
Sear the salmon skin-side down in a hot pan for four minutes without moving it.
Flip, pour in the sauce, and let it bubble and thicken around the fish for three minutes.
Steam the broccoli while that happens.
Serve over rice, spooning the glaze over, with scallions and sesame oil.

title: Chicken Fajitas
blurb: Charred peppers, cumin, and a pan that comes to the table.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Toss the chicken with the spices, half the lime juice and a little oil.
Get a heavy pan very hot. Cook the peppers and onions until they blacken in places, then set aside.
Cook the chicken in the same pan in one layer, undisturbed, until it colours.
Return the vegetables, squeeze over the rest of the lime, and scrape up everything stuck to the pan.
Serve in warm tortillas with sour cream, avocado and cilantro.

title: Chili con Carne
blurb: Better the next day, and the day after that.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Brown the beef in batches so it sears rather than steams. Set it aside.
Soften the onions and pepper, then add the garlic, spices and tomato paste and fry until fragrant.
Return the beef, add the tomatoes and stock, and simmer very gently for an hour.
Add the beans for the last twenty minutes so they keep their shape.
Taste for salt and acid. Serve with rice and sour cream.

title: Pulled Pork Sandwiches
blurb: Low, slow, and then torn apart with two forks.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Rub the pork all over with the paprika, sugar, cumin and salt. Leave it an hour if you have one.
Sear it hard on all sides, then set it on the onions in a covered pot.
Add the tomato paste, vinegar, worcestershire and a splash of water. Cook at 150°C for four hours.
Shred with two forks and stir it back through the reduced liquid.
Dress the cabbage with mayo and vinegar. Pile pork on buns, slaw on top.

title: Chicken Fried Rice
blurb: The reason to make too much rice on purpose.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Get the pan hotter than you think. Scramble the eggs quickly and set them aside.
Sear the chicken until just cooked, then set aside with the eggs.
Fry the carrot, garlic and white parts of the scallions, then add the cold rice and press it into the pan.
Leave it alone for a minute at a time so it toasts rather than steams.
Return everything, add the peas and soy, toss, and finish off the heat with sesame oil and scallion greens.

title: Beef and Broccoli
blurb: Velveted beef, a glossy sauce, and twelve minutes at the stove.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Toss the sliced beef with a tablespoon of the cornstarch and a tablespoon of the soy. Rest 15 minutes.
Blanch the broccoli for 90 seconds and drain it very well.
Sear the beef in a hot pan in one layer, then remove while it is still pink in places.
Fry the garlic and ginger, add the stock, remaining soy, sugar, vinegar and cornstarch slurry.
Once glossy, return the beef and broccoli and toss. Sesame oil off the heat.

title: Sausage and Fennel Pasta
blurb: A sauce that comes together in the time the pasta cooks.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Fry the sausage meat in lumps, breaking it up only once it is well browned.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then the garlic, chili and fennel seeds.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes while the pasta cooks.
Stir in the cream and a ladle of pasta water, then toss the drained pasta through.
Parmesan and basil at the table.

title: Lamb Kofta with Yogurt
blurb: Spiced, charred, and served with something cold and sharp.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Squeeze the water out of the grated onion. This is the difference between kofta and mush.
Mix the lamb with the onion, garlic, spices and chopped herbs. Knead it for a minute so it binds.
Shape around skewers or into fat fingers and chill for 20 minutes.
Grill or pan-fry hard, turning once, until charred outside and just cooked through.
Serve with yogurt whisked with lemon and salt, and warm flatbread.

title: Tuna Melt
blurb: A sandwich that is really a case for browned butter.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Mix the tuna with the mayo, mustard, celery, scallion, capers and lemon. Season well.
Pile onto two slices of bread, cover with cheese, and top with the others.
Butter the outsides generously.
Cook in a covered pan over medium-low heat so the cheese melts before the bread burns.
Press, flip, and cut on the diagonal. It matters.

title: Pepperoni Pizza
blurb: A slow-fermented base and the discipline not to overload it.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Mix flour, yeast, salt and 325 ml water. Knead briefly, then leave overnight in the fridge.
Blitz the tomatoes with the garlic, oregano, oil and salt. Do not cook the sauce.
Divide and shape the dough, leaving the rim untouched so it puffs.
Sauce thinly, then cheese, then pepperoni. Less than you want of all three.
Bake as hot as your oven goes, on a preheated tray or stone, until the crust blisters. Basil after.

title: Chana Masala
blurb: Chickpeas, tomato, and a spice base built properly.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Brown the onions properly — 12 minutes, not 4. This is where the depth comes from.
Add the garlic, ginger and ground spices and fry until the oil separates out.
Add the tomatoes and cook down to a thick paste.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of their liquid and simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few against the side.
Garam masala, lemon and cilantro at the end, off the heat.

title: Mushroom Risotto
blurb: Twenty minutes of stirring, and worth every one of them.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Soak the porcini in a cup of hot stock. That liquid is the best thing in the dish; keep it.
Brown the fresh mushrooms hard in oil, in batches, and set aside. Do not salt them until they colour.
Soften the onion, add the rice and toast it for two minutes until the edges go translucent.
Wine, then stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 18 minutes.
Fold the mushrooms back in, beat in the butter and parmesan off the heat, and rest two minutes before serving.

title: Dal Tadka
blurb: Lentils, and then hot spiced ghee poured over at the last second.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Simmer the lentils with the turmeric and plenty of water for 25 minutes until collapsing. Skim the foam.
Whisk them smooth-ish and season. They should pour, not stand.
For the tadka: heat the butter, add cumin seeds and wait for them to pop.
Add garlic, ginger, onion and chili and fry until the garlic is golden, then the tomato for two minutes.
Pour the whole sizzling lot over the dal at the table. Cilantro, and eat.

title: Falafel Bowl
blurb: Crisp outside, herby green inside, over everything cold and sharp.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.

ingredients.note: dried and soaked — tinned will not hold together

steps: Blitz the soaked chickpeas with the herbs, onion, garlic and spices to a coarse, sandy mix. Do not make a paste.
Stir in the chickpea flour and salt and chill for 30 minutes so it holds.
Shape into small patties and shallow-fry until deeply browned on both sides.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice, a pinch of salt and cold water until it goes pale and loose.
Build bowls: couscous, chopped cucumber and tomato, falafel, and a great deal of tahini sauce.

title: Mapo Tofu
blurb: Numbing, savoury, and faster than ordering it.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Cube the tofu and slide it into salted hot water to warm through while you cook. This stops it breaking up.
Fry the minced mushrooms hard until dry and browned — they are doing the work mince usually does.
Add garlic, ginger, chili and the fermented paste and fry for a minute.
Pour in the stock, then drain and add the tofu. Nudge, do not stir.
Thicken with the cornstarch slurry, then scallions and sesame oil off the heat.

title: Black Bean Burger
blurb: Held together by roasting the beans dry first, not by breadcrumbs.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Drain the beans and roast them dry at 190°C for 15 minutes until the skins split. Wet beans make wet burgers.
Pulse the mushrooms and walnuts and fry them hard until all the water is gone.
Mash two-thirds of the beans, leave a third whole, and mix everything with the panko and spices.
Shape and chill for 20 minutes, then pan-fry in oil for four minutes a side without moving them.
Build with mayo, lettuce and tomato.

title: Cold Peanut Noodles
blurb: Fifteen minutes, mostly whisking.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Cook the noodles, then rinse them under cold water until properly cold.
Whisk the peanut butter with the soy, vinegar, maple, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and sriracha.
It will seize. Add hot water a spoonful at a time until it pours like cream.
Toss the noodles through the sauce with the cucumber.
Scallions, crushed peanuts and lime over the top.

title: Shakshuka
blurb: Eggs poached in a pepper and tomato base, eaten out of the pan.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Cook the peppers and onion slowly in the oil for 15 minutes until genuinely soft.
Add the garlic, spices and harissa and fry for a minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail.
Make wells and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook until the whites set and the yolks do not.
Feta, parsley, bread. Do not plate it.

title: Minestrone
blurb: Whatever is in the drawer, plus beans and a parmesan rind if you have one.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for a full 12 minutes. This is the soup.
Add the garlic, then the tomatoes, and cook until they darken.
Pour in the stock and simmer 20 minutes, then add the beans and zucchini.
Add the pasta and kale for the last 10 minutes.
Finish with olive oil, basil and a splash of vinegar to lift it.

title: Roasted Cauliflower Tacos
blurb: Roasted until the edges go black, with a lime-heavy slaw.
provenance: Written for Kindly. Not copied from any publication.
steps: Break the cauliflower into small florets — small, so there is more edge to char.
Toss with oil, spices and salt and roast at 220°C for 25 minutes without stirring.
Warm the beans with a little of their liquid and mash them roughly.
Dress the cabbage with lime juice, vegan mayo and salt.
Char the tortillas, then build: beans, cauliflower, slaw, avocado, cilantro, more lime.

title: Brothy Porcini Beans with Kale and Garlic Toast
blurb: White beans simmered in a dark mushroom broth until the liquid goes glossy and savoury, with kale wilted in at the end and a slab of oily garlic toast to sit underneath it all.
provenance: Written by Kindly for the craving "something warm and comforting for a cold night". Not a published recipe.

ingredients.note: plus 1 whole clove for the toast
or an extra splash of stock

steps: Put the porcini in a mug or small bowl and pour over 400 ml boiling water. Leave them to soak while you do everything else — 20 minutes is plenty. This liquid is the whole backbone of the dish, so don't tip it away.

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide, heavy pan over high heat. Add the cremini in a single layer and leave them alone for 3-4 minutes. They will release water, look grey and unpromising, then the water cooks off and they start to brown. Wait for that. Stir, cook another 3 minutes until the cut faces are properly dark, then salt them and tip onto a plate.

Turn the heat to medium, add 1 tbsp more oil, and cook the onion and celery with a pinch of salt for 6-7 minutes until soft and just starting to colour at the edges. Add the sliced garlic, thyme and chili flakes and cook 1 minute more, until the garlic smells sweet rather than raw.

Add the tomato paste and fry it, stirring, for a full 2 minutes. It should darken from red to brick and start sticking to the pan. That stuck stuff is flavour. Pour in the red wine and scrape it all up, letting it bubble down until the pan is nearly dry.

Lift the porcini out of their soaking water, squeeze them, and chop them roughly. Add them to the pan. Now pour in the soaking liquid, stopping before the last tablespoon or so — grit settles at the bottom.

Add the beans, stock and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 15 minutes, crushing a few spoonfuls of beans against the side of the pan as you go. That starch is what turns the broth from watery to glossy.

Stir the mushrooms back in with the kale, and cook 4-5 minutes until the kale is dark and tender. Slake the miso with a ladle of the hot broth in a small bowl first, then stir it back into the pan — dropped in whole it will just sit there in lumps. Take the pan off direct high heat once the miso is in; boiling it hard dulls it.

Stir in the vegan butter until it melts into the broth, then a good squeeze of lemon and plenty of black pepper. Taste for salt: stock and miso vary wildly, so this is a real decision, not a formality.

Toast or griddle the bread, rub each hot slice hard with the cut side of the reserved garlic clove, and drizzle with the last of the olive oil. Sit a slice in the bottom of each bowl, ladle the beans over so the bread half-collapses, and scatter with parsley.

title: Smoky Tempeh Carbonara
blurb: Spaghetti tossed in a silken tofu sauce sharp with vegan parmesan and black pepper, with tempeh fried dark and smoky standing in for the pancetta.
provenance: Adapted by Kindly from Spaghetti Carbonara.

ingredients.raw_name: tempeh, sliced thin then cut into short batons
ingredients.note: Thin slices crisp; cubes stay chewy.
Cured bacon is sweet as well as salty.
Tempeh renders no fat of its own, so the pan needs it.
Silken, not soft block tofu — it needs to blend smooth.
Backs up the cheese with the savoury depth the yolks used to bring.
If you have it. It is the whole egg note in one spoon.

steps: Toss the tempeh with the soy sauce, maple syrup, smoked paprika and liquid smoke. Leave it while you get the water on — ten minutes is enough.

Blend the silken tofu with the vegan parmesan, nutritional yeast, black salt if using, turmeric and half the black pepper until completely smooth. It should pour like thick cream; if it doesn't, a splash of water will get it there.

Fry the tempeh in 2 tbsp of the olive oil over medium heat, turning, until the edges go dark and slightly brittle, 5–6 minutes. Unlike bacon, it will not render fat, so start with a hot oiled pan rather than a cold one. Tip the tempeh and its oil into a bowl and take the pan off the heat.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water until just shy of al dente. Reserve a mugful of the water and drain.

Return the pan to low heat with the last tablespoon of oil, add the drained pasta and the tofu sauce, and toss hard, loosening with pasta water a splash at a time until it coats every strand. Keep it on low for a minute — silken tofu wants a little gentle heat to thicken, where egg only wanted residual warmth.
Off the heat, fold through the tempeh and the remaining pepper. Serve at once, with more grated vegan parmesan.

swaps.technique: Slice thin, marinate 10 minutes, then fry in a little oil until the edges go dark.
swaps.flavor_note: Soy sauce, maple syrup, smoked paprika and a drop of liquid smoke. All four, or it will not read as bacon.
swaps.why: Bacon is smoke, salt, sugar and fat — every one of those can be added back.

alternates.why: For dishes where bacon is a crunchy garnish rather than a component.

swaps.technique: For scrambles and custards: blend until smooth, then cook low and slow.
swaps.flavor_note: A pinch of turmeric for colour and black salt (kala namak) for the sulphur note, if you have it.
swaps.why: Silken tofu sets the way egg does when heated gently.

alternates.why: Binds like egg in patties, fritters and batters without adding flavour.

swaps.why: Purpose-made for this and closest on salt.

alternates.why: Cheaper and shelf-stable, with the same savoury hit.

method_notes.text: All four marinade ingredients earn their place: soy for salt, maple for the cure, smoked paprika for colour and liquid smoke for the smell. Drop one and it reads as fried tempeh, not bacon.
The original starts bacon in a cold pan to render fat. Tempeh has none to give, so it goes straight into hot oil and that oil becomes the sauce's fat.
Egg scrambles over direct heat; blended silken tofu does the opposite and only thickens with a minute of low heat. Keep it moving, but keep it on the flame.
Kala namak is sulphurous and smells startling from the jar. Half a teaspoon into the blender is what makes the sauce read as carbonara rather than as a creamy pasta.

title: Toasted Miso Ramen with Charred Scallion Oil
blurb: A deep, savoury bowl built on dried shiitake and kombu, with miso toasted in the pan until it smells like caramel and a slick of blackened scallion oil floating on top.
provenance: Written by Kindly for the craving "ramen". Not a published recipe.

ingredients.note: about 8-10 caps; dried, not fresh — they're the backbone of the broth
dried seaweed, sold with the sushi rice
low-salt if you can, the tare brings plenty
for body — it clouds the broth and gives it a creamy edge
whites for the oil, greens sliced for the top
gochugaru or Aleppo if you have them

ingredients.raw_name: king oyster mushrooms, sliced into thick coins
ingredients.note: cremini or fresh shiitake work too

ingredients.raw_name: extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut in slabs

ingredients.note: fresh if your shop has them, dried blocks if not — discard the sachet

steps: Put the dried shiitake and the kombu in a pot with the vegetable stock. Bring it to a bare shiver — small bubbles at the edge, never a rolling boil. Kombu boiled hard turns slippery and faintly bitter, and you can't take it back. Hold it there 20 minutes, then fish out the kombu. Lift out the shiitake, squeeze them over the pot, slice them thin and keep them for the bowls.

While that steeps, make the scallion oil. Cut the white parts of the scallions into 3cm lengths and put them in a small pan with 5 tbsp neutral oil. Cook over medium heat until the whites are properly blackened at the edges and the oil smells toasty — 6 to 8 minutes, and you want them darker than feels polite. Take the pan off the heat, stir in the chili flakes, and let it sit. It will keep going in the residual heat.

Make the tare. In a bowl, mash the miso, soy sauce, tahini, grated garlic, grated ginger and sesame oil into a smooth paste. This is where all the salt and most of the flavour lives, so it goes in the bowls, not the pot — miso boiled in broth loses its top notes and goes flat.

Get a wide pan very hot with a spoonful of the scallion oil. Lay in the king oyster coins in a single layer and leave them alone for 3 minutes until the undersides are deep brown and lacquered. Flip, brown the other side, then splash in a teaspoon of soy sauce and let it hiss away. Do the same with the tofu slabs if you're using them — dry surface, hot pan, no fiddling. Crowding the pan steams the mushrooms and you lose the browning entirely.
Boil the noodles in a separate pot of unsalted water, one minute shy of the packet time. Never cook them in the broth — the starch they shed will make it cloudy and gluey. Drain and shake them dry.
Warm the corn and wilt the spinach in the hot broth for 30 seconds, then scoop them out.

Divide the tare between four deep bowls, about 2 tbsp each. Ladle in a little hot broth and whisk it into the tare until completely smooth before adding the rest — lumps of miso at the bottom of a bowl are the classic mistake. Taste and adjust with more soy or a few drops of rice vinegar to lift it.

Add the noodles, lifting them so they sit in a neat fold above the broth. Top with the seared mushrooms and tofu, the sliced steeped shiitake, corn, spinach, a big handful of sliced scallion greens, black pepper, and a spoonful of the chili-scallion oil over everything. Eat immediately, while the oil is still pooled on the surface.

title: Smoky Mince Tacos with Lime Cashew Cream
blurb: Twenty minutes, one pan of hard-browned plant mince with cumin and smoked paprika, and everything else goes on the table in bowls.
provenance: Adapted by Kindly from Ground Beef Tacos.

ingredients.note: straight from the fridge, broken into rough clumps
stands in for the salty, meaty fond beef leaves behind
grate or chop finer than you would cheddar
one for the cream, one for the table
more than the original — the mince renders almost no fat of its own

steps: Stir the juice of half a lime and a good pinch of salt into the cashew cream and taste — it should be properly tart, not just rich. Set aside with the rest of the toppings in bowls.

Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat until it shimmers. Add the plant mince in clumps and leave it alone for 3 minutes, then break it up and keep it moving until the edges are dark and crisp — about 5 minutes total, a third less than beef needs. Push it harder than feels right; that crust is the whole point.
Add the onion and cook 3 minutes until soft, then the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chili flakes and tomato paste. Two minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens.
Splash in the soy sauce and about 60 ml water, scrape the pan, and let it reduce for 2 minutes to a glossy sauce that clings.
Warm the tortillas directly over a flame or in a dry pan until they blister. Put the pan and all the bowls on the table and let people build their own.

swaps.technique: Drop straight in where the beef went; it needs about a third less time to brown.
swaps.flavor_note: Brown it harder than feels necessary — that crust is most of what beef was doing.
swaps.why: One-for-one on mass, protein and browning behaviour.

alternates.why: Much cheaper than plant mince and higher in fibre.
Lowest-calorie route, and the one that tastes least like a substitute.

swaps.technique: Melts more reluctantly. Grate finer and cover the pan.
swaps.why: Direct swap where cheddar is melted rather than tasted on its own.

swaps.technique: Blend with lemon juice and salt to taste before using.
swaps.flavor_note: Sour cream is sour. Cashew cream is not, until you make it so — do not skip the lemon.
swaps.why: Matches the richness sour cream was providing.

method_notes.text: Plant mince colours faster than beef and can go from crisp to dry. Five minutes on high heat, undisturbed at first, then broken up.
Beef released its own fat to fry the onion and bloom the spices. Start with two tablespoons of oil instead of a dry pan.
There is no fond, so the soy sauce goes in with the water at the end — it does the salting and the meaty背 note in one move.
Cashew cream is rich but not sour. Lime juice and salt, stirred in before anything else happens, are what make it read as sour cream.
Vegan cheddar melts reluctantly. Grate it fine and scatter it over the hot mince in the pan if you want it molten rather than in a bowl.

title: Chickpea and Walnut Kofta with Yogurt
blurb: Spiced chickpea-and-mushroom fingers charred hard in a pan, served with cold lemony yogurt and warm flatbread.
provenance: Adapted by Kindly from Lamb Kofta with Yogurt.

ingredients.note: two 400 g cans, drained weight; pat dry
the fat that replaces the lamb fat
half in the mix, half in the yogurt

steps: Squeeze the water out of the grated onion with your hands, hard. Do the same with the chopped mushrooms after step 2 — moisture is the difference between kofta and mush.

Fry the mushrooms in 1 tbsp olive oil over high heat, dry pan-style, 6–8 minutes, until they squeak, shrink and start to brown at the edges. No liquid should be left. Scrape into a bowl and cool for 5 minutes.

Mash the chickpeas with a fork or pulse briefly — you want a coarse, uneven paste, not hummus. Add the mushrooms, onion, garlic, tomato paste, walnuts, panko, egg, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, pepper, the parsley and half the mint.

Knead the mixture for a full minute until it tightens and holds a print when you press it. If it feels wet, add another 20 g panko. Shape into 12 fat fingers around skewers or freehand, and chill 20 minutes so they set.

Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan over medium-high — these have no fat to render, so they need the oil to char. Fry 4–5 minutes on the first side without moving them, turn once, and give the second side 3–4 minutes until both faces are dark and crusted.
Whisk the yogurt with the juice of half the lemon, the remaining mint and a good pinch of salt. Serve the kofta with warm flatbread and lemon wedges.

swaps.technique: Sear in chunks, then braise briefly.
swaps.flavor_note: Lamb is carried by cumin, cinnamon and mint more than by the meat. Lean harder on all three.
swaps.why: Sturdy enough for a long-cooked, heavily spiced dish.

method_notes.text: Whole king oyster chunks won't hold a skewer or bind into a finger. They go in chopped and dry-fried as the savoury backbone, with chickpeas and panko doing the structural work.
Two squeeze points: the grated onion, and the mushrooms, which must be cooked until they stop releasing liquid. Skip either and the mixture will slump in the pan.
Toasted walnuts and a generous 2 tbsp of oil in the pan carry the richness. Don't cut the oil — there is no fat rendering out to fry these in.
Cumin, cinnamon and mint are what read as kofta. They're all up slightly on the original, plus smoked paprika for the char note the grill used to supply.
These are softer than meat kofta until the crust forms. Leave them alone for the first 4–5 minutes and turn once, with a thin spatula rather than tongs.
